episode_title: Reframing Affordable Housing For Today’s Market

real_qa.q: What is the Avanath Capital model for giving residents equity incentive in affordable housing?
real_qa.r: Avanath Capital, led by Daryl Carter, created a model where residents receive 5% of their rent payment set aside each month if they pay on time, which accumulates as a down payment fund for future homeownership. This approach reduced turnover costs dramatically—the 5% cost to their bottom line was paid back tenfold because turnover costs were so expensive that the equity incentive wiped out the majority of those turnover expenses.
real_qa.requete: Avanath Capital 5% rent equity model affordable housing

real_qa.q: What are the key features of the Shelby House project in Nashville?
real_qa.r: Shelby House, developed in partnership with Samaritan Recovery Community in Nashville, increased capacity from 50 beds to 132 beds for substance abuse recovery services, while creating 195 affordable housing units next door. Graduates of the recovery program get first access to the most deeply affordable units, and the nonprofit receives recurring income and revenue from the affordable housing without any debt on the new building.
real_qa.requete: Shelby House Nashville Samaritan Recovery 132 beds 195 units

real_qa.q: How does Holliday Ventures incorporate community and services into affordable housing design from day one?
real_qa.r: Holliday Ventures conducts design charrettes with their entire team from day one to determine the building layout, amenities, interiors, and target demographic for each micro neighborhood. For artist housing projects, they create creative amenity spaces where artists can work and bring in nonprofits and local art universities to provide business education services. The approach focuses on creating community support networks that help residents thrive beyond just providing shelter.
real_qa.requete: Holliday Ventures affordable housing design charrettes community amenities

real_qa.q: What percentage of monthly household income should affordable housing cap according to development standards?
real_qa.r: All affordable housing developments cap monthly household living expenses at 30% of income, which allows families to have savings or investment in other areas of raising a family such as food, daycare, transportation, and insurance. This contrasts with current conditions where many families pay 50 to 70% of their monthly paycheck on rent, leaving barely anything for necessities.

real_qa.q: What term does Holliday Ventures use to rebrand affordable housing and why?
real_qa.r: Holliday Ventures uses the term attainable housing instead of affordable housing because it is more palatable and does not carry the negative stigma associated with affordable. The term means the same thing but is an easier way to communicate that they are creating something working class families can attainably afford, and they use this rhetoric in newspaper articles and communications to help rebrand and move away from negative stigmas.
real_qa.requete: attainable housing Holliday Ventures rebrand affordable stigma

real_qa.q: What checks and balances exist in affordable housing programs to prevent misuse of financial incentives?
real_qa.r: Affordable housing programs include multiple layers of oversight: investor checks, state agency checks, local municipality and city checks, and lender checks all monitor compliance with guidelines. Developers surround themselves with counsel who understand tax credit rules, and serious ramifications exist for non-compliance, ensuring developers are held accountable to follow the rules.
real_qa.requete: affordable housing tax credits checks balances compliance oversight
